## Descriptive Statistics (Daily)

```{r summary-daily}
summary_daily <- df_daily %>%
  summarise(
    N        = n(),
    Mean     = round(mean(rain, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Median   = round(median(rain, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    SD       = round(sd(rain, na.rm = TRUE), 3),

```

Daily rainfall is strongly right-skewed (skewness > 3.5) due to many dry days near zero and occasional extreme monsoon events. The mean (6.58 mm/day) far exceeds the median (3.94 mm/day), a typical pattern for tropical precipitation.

Daily data shows high volatility with many zero values and sharp spikes during monsoon events. This noise makes it difficult to model directly, which is one reason for monthly aggregation.

## Histogram dan Distribusi Harian

```{r hist-daily, fig.height=4}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(df_daily$rain, breaks = 60, col = "#4575B4", border = "white",
     main = "Daily Rainfall Distribution", xlab = "mm/day",
     xlim = c(0, 110))

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

The raw distribution is heavily right-skewed. Log transformation substantially reduces skewness and brings the distribution closer to symmetric, which improves fit for parametric models.

# Outlier Analysis (Daily Level)

Outlier analysis is performed on daily data before aggregation. Extreme daily values are caused by real meteorological events (heavy storms, monsoon surges), not measurement errors.

## Identification with IQR

```{r outlier-identify}
Q1            <- quantile(df_daily$rain, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
Q3            <- quantile(df_daily$rain, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
IQR_val       <- IQR(df_daily$rain, na.rm = TRUE)
bound_mild    <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_val
bound_extreme <- Q3 + 3.0 * IQR_val

cat("Q1  :", round(Q1, 2), "mm\n")
cat("Q3  :", round(Q3, 2), "mm\n")
cat("IQR :", round(IQR_val, 2), "mm\n")
cat("Mild outlier threshold (1.5*IQR)   :", round(bound_mild, 2), "mm\n")
cat("Extreme outlier threshold (3.0*IQR):", round(bound_extreme, 2), "mm\n\n")

df_daily <- df_daily %>%
  mutate(outlier_cat = case_when(
    rain > bound_extreme ~ "Extreme",
    rain > bound_mild    ~ "Mild",
    TRUE                 ~ "Normal"
  ))

print(table(df_daily$outlier_cat))
```

The IQR method uses 3x IQR (instead of the standard 1.5x) as the extreme threshold because daily rainfall follows a naturally heavy-tailed distribution. Using 1.5x would flag too many legitimate monsoon events as outliers.

## Visualisasi Outlier

```{r outlier-plot, fig.height=4}
ggplot(df_daily, aes(x = Date, y = rain)) +
  geom_line(color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(data = filter(df_daily, outlier_cat == "Extreme"),
             aes(color = "Extreme"), size = 1.8) +
  geom_point(data = filter(df_daily, outlier_cat == "Mild"),
             aes(color = "Mild"), size = 1.2, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Extreme" = "#D73027", "Mild" = "#FC8D59")) +
  labs(title = "Identified Outliers in Daily Rainfall",
       x = "Date", y = "Rainfall (mm/day)", color = "Outlier") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

## Handling: Winsorizing

Extreme values are capped (Winsorized) at the 3x IQR threshold. This approach:

- Retains all observations (no data deleted)
- Preserves the directional signal of extreme events
- Reduces the disproportionate influence of very high values on model fitting

```{r winsorize}
df_daily <- df_daily %>%
  mutate(rain_clean = ifelse(rain > bound_extreme, bound_extreme, rain))

cat("Cap value (3*IQR bound):", round(bound_extreme, 2), "mm\n")
cat("Values capped          :", sum(df_daily$rain > bound_extreme), "\n")
```

# Weekly Aggregation

All models are fitted on **weekly total rainfall**. The daily data is aggregated into weekly totals to reduce daily noise and better capture seasonal patterns.

```{r weekly-aggregate}
df_weekly <- df_daily %>%
  mutate(
    WEEK_ID = floor(as.numeric(Date - min(Date))/7) + 1
  ) %>%
  group_by(WEEK_ID) %>%
  summarise(
    week_start = min(Date),
    week_end   = max(Date),
    rain_weekly = sum(rain_clean, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(WEEK_ID) %>%
  mutate(
    t = row_number(),
    rain_log = log1p(rain_weekly),

    lag1 = lag(rain_weekly,1),
    lag2 = lag(rain_weekly,2),
    lag3 = lag(rain_weekly,3)
  )

cat("Weekly data:", nrow(df_weekly), "observations\n")

cat(
  "Period:",
  format(min(df_weekly$week_start)),
  "to",
  format(max(df_weekly$week_end)),
  "\n"
)

head(df_weekly)
```

```{r weekly-stats}
summary_weekly <- df_weekly %>%
  summarise(
    N        = n(),
    Mean     = round(mean(rain_weekly), 2),
    Median   = round(median(rain_weekly), 2),
    SD       = round(sd(rain_weekly), 2),
    Min      = round(min(rain_weekly), 2),
    Max      = round(max(rain_weekly), 2),
    Skewness = round(skewness(rain_weekly), 3)
  )

knitr::kable(t(summary_weekly), col.names = "Value",
             caption = "Descriptive statistics of weekly total rainfall (mm/week)")
```

```{r}
Q3_week <- quantile(df_weekly$rain_weekly, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)

bound_extreme_week <- Q3_week + 3.0 * IQR_week
```

## Decomposition Plot

```{r decompose-plot, fig.height=6}
plot(decompose(rain_weekly_ts, type = "additive"))
```

Decomposition separates the series into three components:

- **Trend**: no clear long-term upward or downward drift, consistent with stable climate over 5 years
- **Seasonal**: a strong and consistent annual cycle (S = 52) repeating every year
- **Residual**: the remaining random variation after removing trend and seasonal components

The additive model is appropriate here because the seasonal amplitude (height of the peaks) stays roughly constant across years, rather than growing proportionally with the trend.

## Variance Stationarity

```{r boxcox-weekly}
lambda_weekly <- BoxCox.lambda(rain_weekly_ts + 1)
cat("BoxCox lambda (weekly):", round(lambda_weekly, 4), "\n")
cat("Lambda mendekati 0 -> log transform disarankan\n")
cat("Lambda mendekati 1 -> varians sudah stabil\n\n")

summary(powerTransform(rain_weekly_ts + 1))
```

H0: lambda = 1 (variance stationary). If p-value < 0.05, log transformation is recommended.

## ACF dan PACF (Monthly)

```{r weekly-acf-pacf, fig.height=5}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
acf(rain_weekly_ts, lag.max = 36, main = "ACF - Weekly Rainfall", col = "#2166AC")
pacf(rain_weekly_ts, lag.max = 36, main = "PACF - Weekly Rainfall", col = "#D73027")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

## ADF Test

```{r adf-weekly}
adf_weekly <- adf.test(rain_weekly_ts, alternative = "stationary")
print(adf_weekly)

if (adf_weekly$p.value < 0.05) {
  cat("\np-value < 0.05 -> data STASIONER (d = 0)\n")
} else {
  cat("\np-value > 0.05 -> data TIDAK stasioner -> pertimbangkan differencing (d = 1)\n")
}
```

```{r log-weekly, fig.height=4}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
```

# Train-Test Split

All models use the same 80/20 split on weekly data. The split is sequential (not random) to preserve temporal order.

```{r train-test-monthly}
n_total <- nrow(df_weekly)
n_train   <- floor(0.8 * n_total)
n_test    <- n_total - n_train

train_df <- df_weekly[1:n_train, ]
test_df  <- df_weekly[(n_train+1):n_total, ]

# ts objects
train_weekly_ts <- ts(
  train_df$rain_weekly,
  frequency = 52
)

test_weekly_ts <- ts(
  test_df$rain_weekly,
  frequency = 52
)

train_weekly_log <- ts(
  train_df$rain_log,
  frequency = 52
)

test_weekly_log <- ts(
  test_df$rain_log,
  frequency = 52
)

cat("Total weekly obs :", n_total, "\n")

cat(
  "Train:", n_train, "weeks |",
  format(min(train_df$week_start)),
  "to",
  format(max(train_df$week_end)),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Test :", n_test, "weeks |",
  format(min(test_df$week_start)),
  "to",
  format(max(test_df$week_end)),
  "\n"
)
```

```{r}
c(
  nrow(df_weekly),
  length(train_weekly_ts),
  frequency(train_weekly_ts),
  start(train_weekly_ts),
  end(train_weekly_ts)
)
```

```{r split-plot, fig.height=4}
df_weekly %>%
  mutate(
    Set = ifelse(
      WEEK_ID <= max(train_df$WEEK_ID),

    )
  ) %>%

```

# 9. Modeling

Semua model difit dan dievaluasi pada **data bulanan** (mm/month). Evaluasi menggunakan tiga metrik:

- **RMSE** — sensitif terhadap error besar, unit sama dengan data
- **MAE** — rata-rata besar error, lebih robust terhadap nilai ekstrem
- **MAPE** — error dalam persentase

**catatan:** MAPE dapat tidak stabil ketika nilai aktual mendekati nol, sehingga RMSE dan MAE lebih diutamakan sebagai metrik utama

```{r eval-function}
eval_metrics <- function(actual, predicted, model_name) {
  mask     <- actual > 0
  rmse_val <- rmse(actual, predicted)
  mae_val  <- mean(abs(actual - predicted))
  mape_val <- mean(abs((actual[mask] - predicted[mask]) / actual[mask])) * 100
  cat(model_name, "\n")
  cat("  RMSE:", round(rmse_val, 4), "| MAE:", round(mae_val, 4),
      "| MAPE:", round(mape_val, 2), "%\n\n")
  data.frame(Model = model_name,
             RMSE  = round(rmse_val, 4),
             MAE   = round(mae_val, 4),
             MAPE  = round(mape_val, 2))
}
```

---

## 9.1 Baseline Models

Sebelum model utama, ditetapkan dua **baseline sederhana** sebagai acuan minimum performa. Model yang baik seharusnya mengalahkan baseline ini. Jika tidak, perlu dievaluasi apakah model terlalu kompleks atau data memang sulit diprediksi.

```{r}
snaive_model <- snaive(
  train_weekly_ts,
  h = length(test_weekly_ts)
)

train_fit_snaive <- fitted(snaive_model)

# remove NA caused by first seasonal cycle
valid_idx <- !is.na(train_fit_snaive)

actual_train_snaive <- as.numeric(train_weekly_ts)[valid_idx]
pred_train_snaive   <- as.numeric(train_fit_snaive)[valid_idx]

result_snaive_train <- eval_metrics(
  actual_train_snaive,
  pred_train_snaive,
  "Seasonal Naive (Train)"
)

rmse_snaive_train <- result_snaive_train$RMSE
mae_snaive_train  <- result_snaive_train$MAE
mape_snaive_train <- result_snaive_train$MAPE

pred_test_snaive <- as.numeric(snaive_model$mean)

actual_base <- as.numeric(test_weekly_ts)

result_snaive_test <- eval_metrics(
  actual_base,
  pred_test_snaive,
  "Seasonal Naive (Test)"
)

rmse_snaive <- result_snaive_test$RMSE
mae_snaive  <- result_snaive_test$MAE
mape_snaive <- result_snaive_test$MAPE

cat("\n=== Seasonal Naive ===\n")

cat("\nTrain RMSE :", round(rmse_snaive_train, 4))
cat("\nTrain MAE  :", round(mae_snaive_train, 4))
cat("\nTrain MAPE :", round(mape_snaive_train, 4), "%\n")

cat("\nTest RMSE  :", round(rmse_snaive, 4))
cat("\nTest MAE   :", round(mae_snaive, 4))
cat("\nTest MAPE  :", round(mape_snaive, 4), "%\n")
```
Seasonal Naive sangat relevan untuk data curah hujan karena pola musiman Jakarta sangat kuat dan berulang setiap tahun. Jika model ML tidak mampu mengalahkan Seasonal Naive, itu menandakan model yg lebih kompleks tidak cocok pada dataset ini.

---

## 9.2 Time Series Regression Seasonal (TSR Seasonal)

TSR Seasonal meregresikan curah hujan bulanan terhadap **dummy variabel bulan** dan lag bulan sebelumnya. Setiap koefisien dummy menunjukkan perbedaan rata-rata curah hujan bulan tersebut dibandingkan Januari (baseline/referensi). Misalnya, jika koefisien M2 = +80, artinya Februari rata-rata 80 mm lebih basah dari Januari setelah mengontrol variabel lain.


```{r tsr-setup}
df_train_tsr <- train_df %>%
  mutate(
    WEEK_F = factor(
      ((WEEK_ID - 1) %% 52) + 1
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(lag1),
    !is.na(lag2),
    !is.na(lag3)
  )

cat(
  "Training obs for TSR:",
  nrow(df_train_tsr),
  "\n"
)

str(df_train_tsr)
```

```{r tsr-models}
dummy_vars <- "M2+M3+M4+M5+M6+M7+M8+M9+M10+M11+M12"

m1 <- lm(
  rain_weekly ~ WEEK_F,
  data = df_train_tsr
)

m2 <- lm(
  rain_weekly ~ t + WEEK_F,
  data = df_train_tsr
)

m3 <- lm(
  rain_weekly ~ lag1 + t + WEEK_F,
  data = df_train_tsr
)

m4 <- lm(
  rain_weekly ~ lag1 + lag2 + t + WEEK_F,
  data = df_train_tsr
)

m5 <- lm(
  rain_weekly ~ lag1 + lag2 + lag3 + t + WEEK_F,
  data = df_train_tsr
)
```

```{r tsr-eval-train}
eval_tsr <- function(model, nama, train_data) {
  actual    <- train_data$rain_weekly
  predicted <- fitted(model)
  idx       <- actual > 0
  data.frame(
    Model  = nama,
    Adj_R2 = round(summary(model)$adj.r.squared, 4),
    RMSE   = round(rmse(actual, predicted), 4),
    MAE    = round(mean(abs(actual - predicted)), 4),
    MAPE   = round(mean(abs((actual[idx] - predicted[idx]) / actual[idx])) * 100, 2),
    AIC    = round(AIC(model), 2),
    DW     = round(as.numeric(dwtest(model)$statistic), 4)
  )
}

tabel_tsr <- bind_rows(
  eval_tsr(m1, "Dummy Seasonal Only",           df_train_tsr),
  eval_tsr(m2, "Trend + Dummy",                  df_train_tsr),
  eval_tsr(m3, "Lag1 + Trend + Dummy",           df_train_tsr),
  eval_tsr(m4, "Lag1+Lag2 + Trend + Dummy",      df_train_tsr),
  eval_tsr(m5, "Lag1+Lag2+Lag3 + Trend + Dummy", df_train_tsr)
)
knitr::kable(tabel_tsr, caption = "TSR Seasonal Model Comparison (Training Set)")
```

```{r tsr-best}
best_tsr_idx <- which.min(tabel_tsr$RMSE)
best_tsr     <- list(m1, m2, m3, m4, m5)[[best_tsr_idx]]
cat("Best TSR model:", tabel_tsr$Model[best_tsr_idx], "\n\n")
summary(best_tsr)
```

```{r tsr-vif}
cat("VIF values (best model):\n")
print(round(vif(best_tsr), 2))
cat("\nVIF > 10 = multikolinearitas serius\n")
```

```{r}
#ubah
# ==========================
# Recursive Forecast TSR
# ==========================

h <- nrow(test_df)

yhat_tsr <- numeric(h)

lag1_last <- tail(train_df$rain_weekly, 1)
lag2_last <- tail(train_df$rain_weekly, 2)[1]
lag3_last <- tail(train_df$rain_weekly, 3)[1]

for(i in 1:h){

  row_i <- test_df[i, ]

  row_i$lag1 <- lag1_last
  row_i$lag2 <- lag2_last
  row_i$lag3 <- lag3_last

  row_i$WEEK_F <- factor(
    ((row_i$WEEK_ID - 1) %% 52) + 1,
    levels = levels(df_train_tsr$WEEK_F)
  )

  pred_i <- predict(m5, newdata = row_i)

  yhat_tsr[i] <- pred_i

  lag3_last <- lag2_last
  lag2_last <- lag1_last
  lag1_last <- pred_i
}
```

```{r}
actual_tsr <- test_df$rain_weekly

idx <- actual_tsr > 0

rmse_tsr <- rmse(actual_tsr, yhat_tsr)

mae_tsr <- mae(actual_tsr, yhat_tsr)

mape_tsr <- mean(
  abs(
    (actual_tsr[idx] - yhat_tsr[idx]) /
      actual_tsr[idx]
  )
) * 100

cat(
  "\nTSR Weekly (Recursive Forecast)\n"
)

cat(
  "RMSE:", round(rmse_tsr,4),
  "| MAE:", round(mae_tsr,4),
  "| MAPE:", round(mape_tsr,2), "%\n"
)
```

## 9.3 ARIMA

ARIMA (p,d,q) memodelkan dependensi linier antar observasi melalui komponen AR dan MA. Difit pada **log-transformed monthly data** untuk menstabilkan varians. Forecast dikembalikan ke skala asli dengan `expm1()`.

```{r}
min(train_weekly_ts)

sum(train_weekly_ts <= 0)
```

```{r}
plot(train_weekly_ts)
```


```{r arima-stasioner}
summary(powerTransform(train_weekly_ts + 1))
adf.test(train_weekly_log)

lambda_weekly
```

```{r arima-acf-pacf, fig.height=5}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
acf(
  train_weekly_log,
  lag.max = 104,
  main = "ACF Weekly Rainfall"
)

pacf(
  train_weekly_log,
  lag.max = 104,
  main = "PACF Weekly Rainfall"
)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r}
train_weekly_ts <- ts(
  train_df$rain_weekly,
  start = c(2010, 1),
  frequency = 52
)

test_weekly_ts <- ts(
  test_df$rain_weekly,
  start = c(
    2010 + floor(n_train/52),
    (n_train %% 52) + 1
  ),
  frequency = 52
)

train_weekly_log <- ts(
  train_df$rain_log,
  start = c(2010, 1),
  frequency = 52
)

test_weekly_log <- ts(
  test_df$rain_log,
  start = c(
    2010 + floor(n_train/52),
    (n_train %% 52) + 1
  ),
  frequency = 52
)
```


```{r arima-kandidat}
# ===== Weekly ARIMA Candidates =====

arima_100 <- Arima(train_weekly_log, order = c(1,0,0))
arima_200 <- Arima(train_weekly_log, order = c(2,0,0))
arima_300 <- Arima(train_weekly_log, order = c(3,0,0))

arima_101 <- Arima(train_weekly_log, order = c(1,0,1))
arima_201 <- Arima(train_weekly_log, order = c(2,0,1))
arima_301 <- Arima(train_weekly_log, order = c(3,0,1))

arima_202 <- Arima(train_weekly_log, order = c(2,0,2))
arima_302 <- Arima(train_weekly_log, order = c(3,0,2))
  
arima_aic <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "ARIMA(1,0,0)",
    "ARIMA(2,0,0)",
    "ARIMA(3,0,0)",
    "ARIMA(1,0,1)",
    "ARIMA(2,0,1)",
    "ARIMA(3,0,1)",
    "ARIMA(2,0,2)",
    "ARIMA(3,0,2)"
  ),
  AIC = c(
    AIC(arima_100),
    AIC(arima_200),
    AIC(arima_300),
    AIC(arima_101),
    AIC(arima_201),
    AIC(arima_301),
    AIC(arima_202),
    AIC(arima_302)
  )
)

arima_aic[order(arima_aic$AIC), ]
```

```{r arima-auto}
fit_auto_arima <- auto.arima(train_weekly_log, seasonal = FALSE)
summary(fit_auto_arima)
```

```{r arima-coeftest}
library(lmtest)
coeftest(arima_302)
```

```{r arima-diagnostic}
library(nortest)

e_arima <- residuals(arima_302)

lillie.test(e_arima)

Box.test(
  e_arima,
  lag = 12,
  type = "Ljung-Box"
)

checkresiduals(arima_302)
```

H₀: residual berdistribusi normal
H₁: residual tidak berdistribusi normal

H₀: residual merupakan white noise (tidak ada autokorelasi tersisa)
H₁: residual masih mengandung autokorelasi

```{r arima-best}
best_arima <- arima_302  # ganti sesuai hasil coeftest + diagnostic

# ---- Train performance ----
yhat_arima_train <- expm1(
  as.numeric(fitted(best_arima))
)

actual_arima_train <- as.numeric(
  train_weekly_ts
)

cat(
  "ARIMA RMSE (Train):",
  round(
    rmse(
      actual_arima_train,
      yhat_arima_train
    ),
    4
  ),
  "\n"
)

# ---- Forecast Test ----
fc_arima <- forecast(
  best_arima,
  h = length(test_weekly_ts)
)

# back-transform ke skala asli
yhat_arima_test <- expm1(
  as.numeric(fc_arima$mean)
)

actual_arima_test <- as.numeric(
  test_weekly_ts
)

# ---- Test metrics ----
result_arima <- eval_metrics(
  actual_arima_test,
  yhat_arima_test,
  "ARIMA (Weekly Test)"
)

rmse_arima <- result_arima$RMSE
mae_arima  <- result_arima$MAE
mape_arima <- result_arima$MAPE
```

```{r arima-plot, fig.height=4}
autoplot(train_weekly_log, series = "Training") +
  autolayer(fc_arima, series = "Forecast") +
  autolayer(
    test_weekly_log,
    series = "Actual",
    color = "#D73027"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "ARIMA Forecast vs Actual (Weekly, log scale)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "log(1 + Rainfall)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

```{r arima-residual-analysis, fig.height=8}
resid_arima  <- residuals(best_arima)
fitted_arima <- as.numeric(fitted(best_arima))

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(fitted_arima, resid_arima, pch = 16, col = "#378ADD",
     main = "Residuals vs Fitted - ARIMA",
     xlab = "Fitted (log scale)", ylab = "Residuals")
abline(h = 0, col = "#D73027", lty = 2)

hist(resid_arima, breaks = 15, col = "#74ADD1", border = "white",
     main = "Histogram of Residuals - ARIMA", xlab = "Residuals")

qqnorm(resid_arima, main = "Q-Q Plot - ARIMA Residuals", col = "#378ADD", pch = 16)
qqline(resid_arima, col = "#D73027", lwd = 2)

acf(resid_arima, main = "ACF of Residuals - ARIMA", col = "#2166AC")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r}
# ARIMA train metrics (add to your script)
yhat_arima_train <- expm1(as.numeric(fitted(best_arima)))
actual_train     <- as.numeric(train_weekly_ts)
idx_tr           <- actual_train > 0

cat("ARIMA Train RMSE:", round(rmse(actual_train, yhat_arima_train), 4), "\n")
cat("ARIMA Train MAE :", round(mae(actual_train, yhat_arima_train), 4), "\n")
cat("ARIMA Train MAPE:", round(mean(abs((actual_train[idx_tr] - yhat_arima_train[idx_tr]) /
                                         actual_train[idx_tr])) * 100, 2), "%\n")
```

## 9.4 SARIMA

SARIMA (p,d,q)(P,D,Q)[S] memperluas ARIMA dengan komponen seasonal eksplisit. Dengan data bulanan, seasonal period S = 12. Komponen (P,D,Q) menangkap autokorelasi yang berulang setiap 12 bulan (pola monsoon tahunan).

```{r sarima-acf-pacf-seasonal, fig.height=5}
par(mfrow = c(1,2))

Acf(
  train_weekly_log,
  lag.max = 104,
  main = "ACF - Weekly log(rain)"
)

Pacf(
  train_weekly_log,
  lag.max = 104,
  main = "PACF - Weekly log(rain)"
)

par(mfrow = c(1,1))
```

```{r sarima-kandidat}
library(forecast)

sarima_1 <- Arima(
  train_weekly_log,
  order = c(1,0,0),
  seasonal = list(order = c(1,1,0), period = 52)
)

sarima_2 <- Arima(
  train_weekly_log,
  order = c(2,0,0),
  seasonal = list(order = c(1,1,0), period = 52)
)

sarima_3 <- Arima(
  train_weekly_log,
  order = c(1,0,1),
  seasonal = list(order = c(1,1,0), period = 52)
)

sarima_4 <- Arima(
  train_weekly_log,
  order = c(2,0,1),
  seasonal = list(order = c(1,1,0), period = 52)
)

sarima_5 <- Arima(
  train_weekly_log,
  order = c(1,0,1),
  seasonal = list(order = c(0,1,1), period = 52)
)

sarima_6 <- Arima(
  train_weekly_log,
  order = c(1,0,1),
  seasonal = list(order = c(1,1,1), period = 52)
)

sarima_7 <- Arima(
  train_weekly_log,
  order = c(2,0,2),
  seasonal = list(order = c(1,1,0), period = 52)
)

sarima_8 <- Arima(
  train_weekly_log,
  order = c(2,0,2),
  seasonal = list(order = c(0,1,1), period = 52)
)

sarima_9 <- Arima(
  train_weekly_log,
  order = c(4,0,4),
  seasonal = list(order = c(1,1,0), period = 52)
)

sarima_aic <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "SARIMA(1,0,0)(1,1,0)[52]",
    "SARIMA(2,0,0)(1,1,0)[52]",
    "SARIMA(1,0,1)(1,1,0)[52]",
    "SARIMA(2,0,1)(1,1,0)[52]",
    "SARIMA(1,0,1)(0,1,1)[52]",
    "SARIMA(1,0,1)(1,1,1)[52]",
    "SARIMA(2,0,2)(1,1,0)[52]",
    "SARIMA(2,0,2)(0,1,1)[52]",
    "SARIMA(4,0,4)(1,1,0)[52]"
  ),
  AIC = c(
    AIC(sarima_1),
    AIC(sarima_2),
    AIC(sarima_3),
    AIC(sarima_4),
    AIC(sarima_5),
    AIC(sarima_6),
    AIC(sarima_7),
    AIC(sarima_8),
    AIC(sarima_9)
  )
)

sarima_aic[order(sarima_aic$AIC), ]
```

```{r sarima-auto}
fit_auto_sarima <- auto.arima(
  train_weekly_log,
  seasonal = TRUE
)

summary(fit_auto_sarima)
```

```{r sarima-coeftest}
coeftest(sarima_8)
coeftest(sarima_9)
```

```{r}
# Fit the restricted model: drop ma1, keep ma2 → SARIMA(2,0,1) as approximation
# Actually the cleaner restriction is to fix ma1 = 0
sarima_8_restricted <- Arima(
  train_weekly_log,
  order = c(2, 0, 1),            # q=1 means only one MA term (effectively ma2 renamed ma1)
  seasonal = list(order = c(0, 1, 1), period = 52)
)

cat("Full model    SARIMA(2,0,2)(0,1,1)[52] AIC:", AIC(sarima_8), "\n")
cat("Restricted    SARIMA(2,0,1)(0,1,1)[52] AIC:", AIC(sarima_8_restricted), "\n")
coeftest(sarima_8_restricted)
```

### Diagnostic Checking — Round 1

```{r sarima-diagnostic-1}
library(nortest)

# evaluasi model dengan AIC terbaik terlebih dahulu
e_sarima_8 <- residuals(sarima_8)
cat("=== SARIMA(1,1,1)(0,1,1)12 [AIC terbaik] ===\n")
lillie.test(e_sarima_8)
ljung_8 <- Box.test(e_sarima_8, lag = 52, type = "Ljung-Box")
print(ljung_8)

checkresiduals(sarima_8)
```

Jika Ljung-Box p-value < 0.05, residual belum memenuhi asumsi white noise. Ini berarti masih ada autokorelasi yang belum ditangkap model. Langkah selanjutnya adalah mencoba model dengan ordo yang lebih tinggi untuk menyerap sisa autokorelasi tersebut.


```{r sarima-best}
# gunakan model yang telah diperbaiki
# best_sarima <- best_sarima_improved
best_sarima <- sarima_8
checkresiduals(best_sarima)

# =========================
# TRAIN PERFORMANCE
# =========================
yhat_sarima_train <- expm1(as.numeric(fitted(best_sarima)))
actual_sarima_train <- as.numeric(train_weekly_ts)

cat(
  "\nSARIMA RMSE (train):",
  round(rmse(actual_sarima_train, yhat_sarima_train), 4),
  "\n\n"
)

# =========================
# TEST FORECAST
# =========================
fc_sarima <- forecast(
  best_sarima,
  h = length(test_weekly_ts)
)

yhat_sarima_test <- expm1(as.numeric(fc_sarima$mean))
actual_sarima_test <- as.numeric(test_weekly_ts)

result_sarima <- eval_metrics(
  actual_sarima_test,
  yhat_sarima_test,
  "SARIMA (Test)"
)

rmse_sarima <- result_sarima$RMSE
mae_sarima  <- result_sarima$MAE
mape_sarima <- result_sarima$MAPE

result_sarima
```

## 9.6 Model Comparison Summary

> **Catatan MAPE:** MAPE dapat tidak stabil saat nilai aktual mendekati nol. RMSE dan MAE lebih diutamakan sebagai metrik perbandingan utama.

```{r final-comparison}
# dari Google Collab
rmse_nn_test   <- 33.1963
mae_nn_test    <- 22.6467
mape_nn_test   <- 1614.42
rmse_lstm_test <- 32.4571
mae_lstm_test  <- 23.1068
mape_lstm_test <- 1803.6199951171875
rmse_gru_test  <- 33.478
mae_gru_test   <- 23.4008
mape_gru_test  <- 1450.3499755859375

comparison_table <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Seasonal Naive",
    "TSR Seasonal",
    "ARIMA",
    "SARIMA",
    "Neural Network",
    "LSTM",
    "GRU"
  ),
  RMSE = round(c(
    result_snaive_test$RMSE,
    rmse_tsr, rmse_arima, rmse_sarima,
    rmse_nn_test, rmse_lstm_test, rmse_gru_test
  ), 4),
  MAE = round(c(
    result_snaive_test$MAE,
    mae_tsr, mae_arima, mae_sarima,
    mae_nn_test, mae_lstm_test, mae_gru_test
  ), 4),
  MAPE = round(c(
    result_snaive_test$MAPE,
    mape_tsr, mape_arima, mape_sarima,
    mape_nn_test, mape_lstm_test, mape_gru_test
  ), 2)
)

# order by RMSE (smallest = best)
comparison_table <- comparison_table[
  order(comparison_table$RMSE),
]

knitr::kable(
  comparison_table,
  caption = "Final Model Comparison - Weekly Test Set (Ordered by RMSE)"
)
```

```{r final-plot, fig.height=5}
library(ggplot2)
comp_plot <- comparison_table[!is.na(comparison_table$RMSE), ]

modelCom <- ggplot(comp_plot, aes(x = reorder(Model, RMSE), y = RMSE, fill = RMSE)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(RMSE, 1)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#74ADD1", high = "#D73027") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(comp_plot$RMSE) * 1.2)) +
  labs(title = "Model Comparison - RMSE on Weekly Test Set",
       subtitle = "Lower RMSE = better | Baseline models shown for reference",
       x = NULL, y = "RMSE (mm/week)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "none")
```
